seoTitle: Typeform Tutorial for Beginners: Getting Started Guide
metaDescription: A beginner's walkthrough of Typeform covering your first form, workflow branching, automations, and sharing to collect responses.
intro: Typeform's account is friendlier than most form builders on first login, but a blank workspace still leaves a beginner guessing where design ends and logic begins. It's also not obvious where the newer AI-assisted tools fit in. This tutorial walks through starting from an empty workspace, building a form's branching workflow, and connecting automations so responses go somewhere useful the moment they arrive. Those pieces matter more than which color theme you pick, and they're where most of Typeform's real complexity hides.
costNote: The free plan covers everything in this guide, including branching and one automation. It caps monthly form responses, shown as a running counter in My workspace, so heavy testing or real traffic may eventually push you toward a paid plan.

steps.heading: Start from My workspace
steps.body: Every new account lands on My workspace, which is also where every form you build will live. Typeform surfaces AI-suggested starting points at the top: cards like "Monitor project milestones and team updates" or "Organize tasks and deadlines," each with a one-click Use this form button that clones a ready-made structure instead of a blank question list. A running counter on the left tracks your free-tier response limit. Note it from day one, since it caps how much real testing you can do before deciding on a paid plan.

image.caption: My workspace on a fresh account — AI-suggested form templates at the top, a free-tier response counter on the left, and Create form to start from scratch.

steps.heading: Build out the question flow
steps.body: Click Create form, or Use this form on a suggested template, to open the Content editor. Questions are added through the Add content panel and reordered by dragging them in the left-hand list. Every question type, from Multiple Choice and Rating to Long Text and Payment, configures inline once you add it, so a working question set comes together without leaving the editor screen. Beginners tend to over-ask. A form that answers one clear purpose with six well-chosen questions consistently completes better than one trying to capture everything at once.

steps.heading: Wire up branching in the Workflow tab
steps.body: The Workflow tab is where Typeform's real power shows. It renders the form as a chain of connected question nodes, with a Logic panel controlling which question a respondent sees next based on how they answered the last one. Typeform folded what used to be a separate Logic tab into this Workflow view, so older guides that mention a standalone Logic tab are describing an earlier layout. A recent update also lets you start a branching rule straight from a question in the builder, without opening Workflow at all. A sidebar on the right lists what else you can attach to the flow: Connect actions that pull data into spreadsheets on submission, Automations that trigger based on form activity, and Contacts mapping that turns form fields into CRM-style records. Skip this tab and every respondent sees the same sequence, regardless of what they've already told you.

image.caption: The Workflow tab's branching view — a connected chain of question nodes, with Connect, Automations, and Contacts panels on the right for wiring up what happens after submission.

steps.heading: Set up an automation for new submissions
steps.body: Under Automations, Create automation lets you define what happens the moment a response comes in. The panel tracks Form submissions and Contact activity or updates as trigger types, with more specific triggers marked Coming soon as Typeform builds the feature out further. Even a beginner setup, like emailing yourself on every new submission, means you stop manually checking the Results tab to know something came in. Do this before the form goes live, not after. A form with no automation just becomes a dashboard nobody remembers to check.

image.caption: The Automations tab: Create automation alongside trigger types like Form submissions and Contact activity/updates for reacting to new responses automatically.

steps.heading: Use the AI assistant, and know it now builds automations too
steps.body: Typeform's AI tools sit inside the editor as a chat-style assistant, labeled Chat to create or Ask Typeform AI depending on where you access it, and it can draft a set of questions from a plain-language description of what you're trying to learn. Typeform has extended this beyond question drafting: you can now prompt the assistant to build automated workflows too, things like managing contacts, sending follow-ups, or nurturing leads, without setting each one up by hand in the Workflow tab. Treat any AI-generated output as a first draft. Review every question and every automation it proposes for tone and relevance, since it doesn't know your audience the way you do.

steps.heading: Preview, then publish and share
steps.body: Before publishing, click through the form in Preview mode as a respondent would, testing any branching paths you set up in Workflow to confirm each answer routes correctly. Once it checks out, publish from the Share tab, where you'll find the direct link plus separate embed options for email and web pages. The link stays stable through future edits, so anywhere you share it now keeps working as you refine questions later.

troubleshooting.problem: A guide or tutorial mentions a separate Logic tab that isn't in the editor anymore.
troubleshooting.cause: Typeform folded the old Logic tab into the newer Workflow tab, which now also holds Connect, Automations, and Contacts in one place.
troubleshooting.fix: Open Workflow instead of looking for Logic on its own. The branching controls are inside it, and can also be started directly from a question in the builder.

troubleshooting.problem: An AI-drafted automation does something you didn't ask for.
troubleshooting.cause: Typeform AI now builds automated workflows, like contact management or follow-ups, from a plain-language prompt, not just question sets, so a vague prompt can produce a broader automation than intended.
troubleshooting.fix: Review any AI-generated automation in the Workflow tab before publishing, the same way you'd review AI-drafted questions.

faq.question: Is Typeform free to start with?
faq.answer: Yes. The free plan builds and publishes forms, but it caps monthly responses, shown as a running counter in your workspace. That's enough to test a form before deciding on a paid plan.

faq.question: Do I need design experience to make a good-looking form?
faq.answer: No. Typeform's built-in themes and AI-suggested templates handle most of the visual work, so you can adjust colors and branding without designing a layout from scratch.

faq.question: What is Typeform's Workflow tab used for?
faq.answer: It's where you set branching logic, which used to live in a separate Logic tab before Typeform folded it into Workflow, plus where you connect Automations and Contacts so form activity triggers actions elsewhere.

faq.question: Where did the Logic tab go?
faq.answer: It's now part of Workflow. Typeform merged Logic into a broader Workflow view that also covers Connect, Automations, and Contacts, and you can start a branching rule directly from a question in the builder without opening it separately.

faq.question: Can beginners use Typeform's AI features right away?
faq.answer: Yes. The AI assistant is built into the editor and can draft questions, and now automated workflows too, like contact follow-ups, from a plain description of your goal. Review its output before publishing, since it won't automatically match your audience's tone.

faq.question: What's the difference between Automations and Workflow branching?
faq.answer: Workflow branching controls what the respondent sees next inside the form itself. Automations run after a response is submitted, sending a notification, updating a contact record, and live inside the same Workflow tab instead of a separate part of the editor.
